questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Each item consists of a sentence with an underlined word followed by four words. Select the word that is opposite in meaning to the underlined word.

During the trial, the witness's deposition was __equivocal__.
questions.explanation:
Concept: equivocal means ambiguous or open to more than one meaning.
Step 1: ambiguous, evasive and guarded are close in meaning to it.
Step 2: the opposite is explicit (clear and direct).
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2026 General Ability Test set A, Part A English (set code TFDD-B-AGT – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.theme: Findings resisted because they challenged assumptions
questions.question:
Directions: Reorder the PQRS set to create the most appropriate meaningful sentence.

The findings were
P: that had long been accepted
Q: because they fundamentally challenged the assumptions
R: met with considerable resistance at first
S: by the mainstream scientific community
The proper sequencing should be:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: the sentence starts with 'The findings were' and R completes the verb: 'met with considerable resistance at first'.
Step 2: Q gives the reason ('because they fundamentally challenged the assumptions') and P qualifies it ('that had long been accepted').
Step 3: S closes it: '...accepted by the mainstream scientific community'.
Order: RQPS.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2026 General Ability Test set A, Part A English (set code TFDD-B-AGT – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.theme: Achievements as product of sustained effort
questions.question:
Directions: Reorder the PQRS set to create the most appropriate meaningful sentence.

It is often argued that
P: are not the result of innate talent alone
Q: but rather the product of
R: extraordinary achievements
S: sustained effort and deliberate practice
The proper sequencing should be:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: R is the subject ('extraordinary achievements') and P is its predicate ('are not the result of innate talent alone').
Step 2: Q ('but rather the product of') leads to S ('sustained effort and deliberate practice').
Order: RPQS.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2026 General Ability Test set A, Part A English (set code TFDD-B-AGT – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.question:
Directions: Reorder the PQRS set to create the most appropriate meaningful sentence.

The historian noted that
P: had been systematically erased
Q: the memory of certain communities
R: and replaced with a sanitized narrative
S: from the official records of the colonial period
The proper sequencing should be:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Q is the subject and P its verb: 'the memory of certain communities had been systematically erased'.
Step 2: S gives the place ('from the official records of the colonial period') and R adds the second action ('and replaced with a sanitized narrative').
Order: QPSR.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2026 General Ability Test set A, Part A English (set code TFDD-B-AGT – A)

questions.subject: Sentence Organisation
questions.theme: Literature's power lies in disturbing assumptions
questions.question:
Directions: Reorder the PQRS set to create the most appropriate meaningful sentence.

Critics have long maintained that
P: literature's true power lies in its
Q: assumptions and not in the mere
R: ability to disturb comfortable
S: reproduction of social reality
The proper sequencing should be:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: P starts the clause ('literature's true power lies in its'), R completes 'ability to disturb comfortable', Q finishes the object ('assumptions').
Step 2: Q continues with 'and not in the mere', followed by S ('reproduction of social reality').
Order: PRQS.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2026 General Ability Test set A, Part A English (set code TFDD-B-AGT – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question: Directions: The following items have four sentences, one of which is grammatically correct. Select the most appropriate correct sentence.
questions.opt_a: She insisted that he apologises immediately.
questions.opt_b: She insisted that he apologise immediately.
questions.opt_c: She insisted that he may apologise immediately.
questions.opt_d: She insisted that he apologised immediately.
questions.explanation:
Concept: verbs like insist, demand, suggest take the subjunctive (base form) in the that-clause when they express a demand.
Step 1: 'insisted that he apologise' is correct.
Step 2: the other options use the wrong verb form or an unwanted modal.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2026 General Ability Test set A, Part A English (set code TFDD-B-AGT – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.theme: Tense with last night and police as plural
questions.question: Directions: The following items have four sentences, one of which is grammatically correct. Select the most appropriate correct sentence.
questions.opt_a: The police has arrested the accused last night.
questions.opt_b: The police have arrested the accused last night.
questions.opt_c: The police arrested the accused last night.
questions.opt_d: The police had arrested the accused last night.
questions.explanation:
Concept: police is a plural noun, and a definite past time marker (last night) needs the simple past.
Step 1: 'has' fails agreement; 'have arrested' (present perfect) fails with last night.
Step 2: 'had arrested' needs a later past reference.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2026 General Ability Test set A, Part A English (set code TFDD-B-AGT – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.question: Directions: The following items have four sentences, one of which is grammatically correct. Select the most appropriate correct sentence.
questions.opt_a: The teacher made the students to rewrite the essay.
questions.opt_b: The teacher has the students to rewrite the essay.
questions.opt_c: The teacher got the students rewriting the essay.
questions.opt_d: The teacher had the students rewrite the essay.
questions.explanation:
Concept: causative 'had/made + object + base verb' (no 'to'); 'got' takes 'to + verb'.
Step 1: (a) wrongly adds 'to' after made; (b) has the same error; (c) is not idiomatic.
Step 2: 'had the students rewrite' is correct.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2026 General Ability Test set A, Part A English (set code TFDD-B-AGT – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.theme: Preposition and word order in an indirect question
questions.question: Directions: The following items have four sentences, one of which is grammatically correct. Select the most appropriate correct sentence.
questions.opt_a: I shall base my decision on how much free time can I manage.
questions.opt_b: I shall base my decision about how much free time I can manage.
questions.opt_c: I shall base my decision on how much free time I can manage.
questions.opt_d: I shall base my decision to how much free time I can manage.
questions.explanation:
Concept: 'base on' is the correct collocation, and an embedded question keeps statement word order.
Step 1: (a) inverts the order; (b) and (d) use the wrong preposition.
Step 2: (c) is correct.
Answer: (c)
questions.source: NDA II 2026 General Ability Test set A, Part A English (set code TFDD-B-AGT – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.theme: Article and verb in a because-clause
questions.question: Directions: The following items have four sentences, one of which is grammatically correct. Select the most appropriate correct sentence.
questions.opt_a: Do not panic because a situation is under control.
questions.opt_b: Do not panic because situation under control.
questions.opt_c: Do not panic however a situation is under control.
questions.opt_d: Do not panic because the situation is under control.
questions.explanation:
Concept: a specific situation needs the definite article, and a clause needs a finite verb.
Step 1: (a) uses 'a' where the context points to a known situation; (b) lacks article and verb; (c) uses the wrong connector.
Step 2: (d) is complete and correct.
Answer: (d)
questions.source: NDA II 2026 General Ability Test set A, Part A English (set code TFDD-B-AGT – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.topic: Active and Passive Voice / Direct and Indirect Speech
questions.theme: Passive of linking verb and imperative
questions.question:
Directions: Read the following pairs. Identify the pair(s) wherein the Passive Voice is correctly stated.

Read the following pairs:
I. Active: These grapes taste sour. | Passive: These grapes are sour when they are tasted.
II. Active: Forget the past. | Passive: Let the past be forgotten.
questions.explanation:
Concept: 'taste sour' uses taste as a linking verb, which has no true passive; 'are sour when they are tasted' changes the meaning.
Pair II: the passive of an imperative is 'Let + object + be + past participle', so 'Let the past be forgotten' is correct.
Answer: (b)
questions.source: NDA II 2026 General Ability Test set A, Part A English (set code TFDD-B-AGT – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.topic: Active and Passive Voice / Direct and Indirect Speech
questions.question:
Directions: Read the following pairs. Identify the pair(s) wherein the Passive Voice is correctly stated.

Read the following pairs:
I. Active: They asked me my name. | Passive: My name was asked by them.
II. Active: They found him guilty. | Passive: He found them guilty.
questions.explanation:
Pair I: with two objects, one can become the subject; 'My name was asked by them' keeps the meaning, so it is acceptable.
Pair II: 'He found them guilty' reverses the doer and the receiver, so it is not a passive of the active sentence (it should be 'He was found guilty by them').
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2026 General Ability Test set A, Part A English (set code TFDD-B-AGT – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.topic: Active and Passive Voice / Direct and Indirect Speech
questions.question:
Directions: Read the following pairs. Identify the pair(s) wherein the Indirect Speech is correctly stated.

Read the following pairs:
I. Direct: He said, "Bravo! You have written the best answer." | Indirect: He applauded him saying that he had written the best answer.
II. Direct: "The sun rises in the East," said the teacher. | Indirect: The teacher said that the sun rose in the East.
questions.explanation:
Pair I: 'Bravo!' becomes 'applauded', and the present perfect becomes past perfect: correct.
Pair II: a universal truth keeps the present tense ('the sun rises'), so changing it to 'rose' is wrong.
Answer: (a)
questions.source: NDA II 2026 General Ability Test set A, Part A English (set code TFDD-B-AGT – A)

questions.subject: Grammar and Usage
questions.topic: Active and Passive Voice / Direct and Indirect Speech
questions.theme: Imperative and exclamation in reported speech
questions.question:
Directions: Read the following pairs. Identify the pair(s) wherein the Indirect Speech is correctly stated.

Read the following pairs:
I. Direct: He said to him, "Wait here until I return." | Indirect: He ordered him to wait here until he returned.
II. Direct: He said, "Alas! I am undone." | Indirect: He exclaimed sadly that he was undone.
questions.explanation:
Pair I: when reporting, 'here' normally changes to 'there' ('wait there until he returned'), so leaving 'here' is an error.
Pair II: 'Alas!' becomes 'exclaimed sadly', and 'am' becomes 'was': correct.
Answer: (b). Medium confidence: it depends on the setter treating 'here' as an error.
questions.source: NDA II 2026 General Ability Test set A, Part A English (set code TFDD-B-AGT – A)

questions.subject: Vocabulary
questions.question:
Directions: Read the following pairs. Identify the pairs wherein the one word substitution is correctly stated.

Read the following pairs:
I. One who studies handwriting: Graphologist
II. One who draws maps: Cartographer
III. One who studies flags: Vexillologist
questions.explanation:
Graphologist studies handwriting; a cartographer draws maps; a vexillologist studies flags.
All three are correct.
Answer: (d)

questions.question:
Directions: Read the following pairs. Identify the pair(s) wherein the one word substitution is correctly stated.

Read the following pairs:
I. One who knows everything: Omnipotent
II. One who is all powerful: Omniscient
III. One who abandons religious faith: Apostate
questions.explanation:
Omniscient means all-knowing and omnipotent means all-powerful, so I and II are swapped and wrong.
An apostate is one who abandons religious faith: III is correct.
Answer: (c)
